notes: The 'no connection' warning on microbit1 is not a real problem for this manual, so I kept the graph unchanged. The tutorial involves exactly one physical part, the micro:bit, and nothing for it to connect to.

The game runs entirely in software (MakeCode blocks). It uses only the micro:bit's own on-board buttons A and B and its on-board LED display. These are inside the one part and are not catalogue ports (the card lists only 0, 1, 2, 3V, GND), so no edge can describe them.
The tutorial has no wires, breadboard, external LEDs or buttons. Adding any of them to force an edge would break the rule to use exactly the parts the tutorial lists.
A USB cable or computer would be needed to power and program the board, but the tutorial doesn't list either as a part. I didn't invent one to create a connection.
The 'while not A and not B' loop and the 'if A / if B' blocks are program logic, not physical connections, so they don't appear as edges.
